title: CohypomonotoneAdjoint.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained nonlinear root finding for a globally cohypomonotone operator F:E→E. A zero xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. No scalar objective or saddle representation is required.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: One exact oracle returns either F(x) or the adjoint derivative product J(x)*w. Both query types consume one call from the same fixed budget. Replies are exact for every call index and seed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CohypomonotoneAdjoint.lean: spec.Query and the first three clauses of spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space; the norm and derivative operator norm use this geometry.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: F is differentiable everywhere, ‖F(x)−F(y)‖≤L‖x−y‖, and ‖J(x)−J(y)‖≤L₂‖x−y‖. Global cohypomonotonicity requires ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥−ρ‖F(x)−F(y)‖², with no upper restriction on ρL. Valid parameters satisfy L>0, L₂≥0, ρ≥0, R≥0, ε>0. E,L,L₂,ρ,x0 are public; R and ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor, and xstar is existential.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CohypomonotoneAdjoint.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The residual bound must hold almost surely under the joint law of algorithm and oracle seeds after execution with the supplied fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy the unsquared operator residual bound ‖F(output)‖≤ε. No averaging, best-iterate, or last-iterate output restriction is specified.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Cohypomonotone root finding with unrestricted ρL, a globally Lipschitz derivative, exact adjoint derivative products, and hidden radius and accuracy parameters is a meaningful specialized oracle formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Cohypomonotone Root Finding with Adjoints

We seek a zero of a differentiable map F:E→E on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The map is L-Lipschitz and ρ-cohypomonotone, and its derivative J(x):E→E is L2-Lipschitz, where L>0, L2≥0, and ρ≥0. A given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a zero. The oracle returns F(x) or the adjoint product J(x)∗w for x,w∈E. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying ∥F(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The root-finding problem is to find x∈E such that F(x)=0. The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives only E, L, L2, ρ, and x0; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Differentiability and Lipschitz bounds). The map F is Fréchet differentiable at every x∈E, with derivative J(x). For every x,y∈E, ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥J(x)−J(y)∥op≤L2∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Cohypomonotonicity). For every x,y∈E, ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥−ρ∥F(x)−F(y)∥2.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance to a zero). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)=0,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Oracle queries may use any x,w∈E. Both reply types are exact, with the adjoint characterized by ⟨J(x)∗w,h⟩=⟨w,J(x)h⟩,h∈E. Each evaluation of F(x) or J(x)∗w counts as one call toward a shared oracle-call budget. After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy ∥F(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, F:E→E is differentiable and L-Lipschitz, with L2-Lipschitz Jacobian and ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥−ρ∥F(x)−F(y)∥2. A zero x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, where L>0 and L2,ρ,R≥0. Exact queries return F(x) or DF(x)∗w. The target is ∥F(x^)∥≤ε, ε>0, almost surely; the constructed algorithms are deterministic. Their updates use L,L2,ρ; R,ε enter their budgets. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

(3) Inexact Halpern (Alacaoglu et al. 2026), Thm. 2.1, Cor. 2.2; G=0, ρL<1 O(1+T/ddlog⁡(e+T/d)) F calls; η=(ρ+1/L)/2 (1), (2): Scope extends to every ρ with adjoints and Lipschitz Jacobian. On d>0, cost becomes O(1+T+(L2R/L)ℓ2). For L=R=L2=1, d=10−2, ε≤10−2: O(ε−1+ℓ2) versus O(104ε−1log⁡(e+100/ε)). (1), (2) need adjoints and known L2; add (L2R/L)ℓ2 burn-in. This can dominate for larger ε. No general G extension.
(4) EAG (Yoon and Ryu 2021), Cor. 1 and monotone-operator extension; ρ=0 O(1+LR/ε) F calls (1), (2): No established improvement on ρ=0; scope extends to ρ>0 with the stronger oracle and Jacobian regularity. (1), (2) add (L2R/L)ℓ2 and require adjoints and known Lipschitz-Jacobian constant L2.

Within this realization, (1) versus (2) removes a leading 1+ρL factor for ρL≥1, ε(1+ρL)4L2ℓ2≪L2. (1), (2) require Lipschitz F and Jacobian. Internally, (1) versus (2) increases burn-in by (1+ρL)log⁡(e+ρL); no uniform dominance.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Defs

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CohypomonotoneAdjoint

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  L : ℝ
  L₂ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.finiteE

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → p.E
  Query p := p.E ⊕ (p.E × p.E)
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.L₂ ∧ 0 ≤ q.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q F oracle :=
    ∃ J : q.E → q.E →L[ℝ] q.E,
      (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl x)) seed = F x) ∧
      (∀ k seed x w h, ⟪oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr (x, w))) seed, h⟫ = ⟪w, J x h⟫) ∧
      (∀ x, HasFDerivAt F (J x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖J x - J y‖ ≤ q.L₂ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖F x - F y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x y, -q.ρ * ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ ⟪F x - F y, x - y⟫) ∧
      (∃ xstar, F xstar = 0 ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q F output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), ‖F (output ω)‖ ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CohypomonotoneAdjoint
